recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It narrowly corrects the already-applied FHIR-52919 search parameters to satisfy the same-operation composite behavior without adding unrelated parameters.
issue_request: FHIR-52919 was Applied/Persuasive for R6 by BR&R. It requested search parameters for MedicinalProductDefinition.operation.organization and MedicinalProductDefinition.operation.type, plus composite parameters that support querying organization and operation type together on the same instance.
initial_application: Upstream commit e444f101fb2f66bcd3b344bdd3cb37c250c54d3b added the operation organization/type search parameters and composites. Follow-up commits e4145c69af4693704a3cb3df7188c5c96728bb32 and e23a5d1fbec9ed11ff9d179f1fef4a1d91583fa4 added the reference targets. The applied composites still evaluated against the whole resource and used search-parameter codes as component sub-expressions.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively registers medicinalproductdefinition as a current resource, so the MedicinalProductDefinition search-parameter bundle is in build scope. SearchParameter.component.expression is a sub-expression relative to the composite SearchParameter.expression, so same-operation matching requires the parent expression to select MedicinalProductDefinition.operation and the component expressions to be relative operation children.
reconciliation: Changed both operation organization/type composites to use MedicinalProductDefinition.operation as the composite expression, organization as the organization component expression, and type.reference/type.concept as the operation type component expressions. The component definitions now point to operation-type and operation-type-code.
source_changes: source/medicinalproductdefinition/bundle-MedicinalProductDefinition-search-params.xml: scoped operation-organization-type and operation-organization-type-code composites to MedicinalProductDefinition.operation and corrected their component definitions/relative expressions.
